court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Joint Civil Judge Junior Division, Aurangabad, Hindu Marriage Petition No.114 of 2011
case_name: Kamod Shrihari Deshpande vs Madhuri Kamod Deshpande

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Kamod Shrihari Deshpande, husband, private service
parties.respondent_defendant: Madhuri W/o Kamod Deshpande, wife, household

facts_of_case: The parties were married and the husband instituted a petition for dissolution of marriage under Section 13(i)(a), 13(1)(iii), 13(i-b) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The wife failed to appear and the petition proceeded ex-parte. The trial court allowed the petition and declared the marriage dissolved.

legal_principles.principle: An appeal shall ordinarily lie from the decisions of the Court.
legal_principles.held: In terms of Section 28(1) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, the appeal shall ordinarily lie from the decisions of the Court.

legal_principles.principle: The District Court shall be the Court of Appeal from all decrees and orders passed by the subordinate Courts.
legal_principles.held: In terms of Section 8 of the Maharashtra Civil Courts Act, the District Court shall be the Court of Appeal from all decrees and orders passed by the subordinate Courts.

outcome.final_order: The appeal was allowed with directions about appointment of guardian / next friend for the respondent-wife and thereafter the petition
